text: To cut a given circumference in half. Let $ADB$ be the given circumference. So it is required to cut circumference $ADB$ in half.
and let it be cut in half at (point) $C$ [Prop.~1.10].
And let $CD$ be drawn from point $C$, at right-angles to $AB$ [Prop.~1.11].
And since $AC$ is equal to $CB$, and $CD$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AC$, $CD$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BC$, $CD$ (respectively).
assertion: the two straight-lines AC, CD equal the two straight-lines BC, CD respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $AC$, $CD$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $BC$, $CD$ (respectively)

text: And angle $ACD$ (is) equal to angle $BCD$. For (they are) each right-angles.
Thus, the base $AD$ is equal to the base $DB$ [Prop.~1.4].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the base $AD$ is equal to the base $DB$

text: And equal straight-lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater (circumference being equal) to the greater, and the lesser to the lesser [Prop.~1.28].
assertion: equal straight-lines cut off equal circumferences, greater to greater and lesser to lesser

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: equal straight-lines cut off equal circumferences, the greater (circumference being equal) to the greater, and the lesser to the lesser

text: And the circumferences $AD$ and $DB$ are each less than a semi-circle.
assertion: circumferences AD and DB are each less than a semi-circle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the circumferences $AD$ and $DB$ are each less than a semi-circle

text: Thus, the given circumference has been cut in half at point $D$. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
